Craving an escape into a landscape that feels almost otherworldly? In the heart of Transylvania, there’s a hidden haven where nature’s splendor is on full display. Imagine standing amidst the towering Carpathian Mountains, their rugged peaks often kissed by clouds, offering a majestic and serene backdrop. This isn’t just scenery; it’s an immersive experience where every vista tells a story of timeless beauty and tranquility. Transylvania’s rolling hills and expansive valleys are a feast for the eyes. In spring and summer, the meadows burst into vibrant colors, blanketed with wildflowers that sway gently in the breeze. The forests here are ancient, filled with towering trees and crisscrossed by crystal-clear streams that sparkle in the sunlight. Each trail you take unveils new panoramas – from sun-dappled clearings to sweeping views that stretch across miles of untouched wilderness. The air is filled with the fresh scent of pine and earth, and the silence is profound, broken only by the rustle of leaves and the distant murmur of streams. As you explore, you’ll encounter some of the most breathtaking lookout points. Imagine the sense of awe as you stand on a secluded plateau, gazing out over a sea of green that seems to go on forever, framed by the dramatic silhouettes of the Carpathian peaks. Whether you’re hiking along scenic trails, resting by a mountain stream, or simply soaking in the panoramic vistas from a quiet hilltop, every moment here is a reminder of nature’s raw and untouched beauty. How does this place make you feel about the simple, unadulterated wonders of the world? I wanted to give this plain front yard a premium upgrade, so I grabbed my tools and got to work! Watching the real progress unfold in this timelapse is incredibly satisfying. Here is a step-by-step breakdown of how I built this modern rock garden: 1️⃣ First, I mapped out a smooth, curved border on the grass using white spray paint. 2️⃣ Next, I dug out the edge along the line and laid down a heavy-duty black weed barrier. 3️⃣ I installed a sleek stone border, block by block, to keep everything neat and contained. 4️⃣ Then came the best part—pouring and leveling tons of crisp white river rocks for that beautiful, high-contrast look. 5️⃣ Finally, I styled the space by placing a dark statement sphere, planting some architectural agaves, and adding solar pathway lights. Seeing the before and after of this build progress makes all the hard work totally worth it! 21 hours in 90 seconds👨🏽‍🌾 ⚠️Flash Warning⚠️ This house was bought near the end of 2025 and the garden was a right state!  I was called in to replace the fence panels and totally rip out the garden  (not the posts, they are a bit crooked but they are still standing😅)  I started with the fence panels, then began to totally clear the area of weeds and any other debris in the garden.  We added 2 railway sleepers at the back for a little flower bed. Then a thick layer of top soil was spread and we rolled out the turf. Then we moved 4 tonnes of hardcore to the back through the house!  Backbreaking stuff.  Thanks to my pal @Wagwarn Abel for jumping on and giving me a hand 🙏 This is obviously unfinished but I think the owner was going to slab the rest himself, so our job is done here for now! As always I wanna know what would YOU do now? There's a bed at the back that's totally empty!  I read and appreciate any comments and genuinely like reading your suggestions🙏 Thanks so much for watching anyway, follow if you haven't already for more vids like this!! Five plants that separate a designed garden from a planted one. Rosemary — most people treat it as a herb. Designers use it as a structural evergreen with silver foliage, late winter bloom, and serious drought tolerance once established. Echinops — steel-blue globe thistle that holds its form into winter. Pollinators love it, it seeds around just enough, and nothing else gives you that texture. White Cloud Nepeta — all the soft billowing habit of catmint, none of the blue. Cleaner in a white or silver palette. Underused because most people don’t know it exists. Mountain Hydrangea (Hydrangea serrata) — more refined than arborescens, lacecap form, better fall color, and it actually performs in part shade without flopping. Blue Mist Fothergilla (Fothergilla gardenii ‘Blue Mist’) — blue-green foliage all season, then flame in fall. Native, compact, and genuinely beautiful. The plant that makes clients ask “what is that?” #gardendesign #landscapedesign
